title: Affine pointed neighbourhoods are cofinal
statement:
The full subcategory of affine [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] pointed
etale neighborhoods is initial in $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], hence cofinal for the
opposite-indexed stalk colimit.

proof.text: For every pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$, the affine-shrink lemma gives an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V_0,\bar v_0)$ and a point-preserving morphism $(V_0,\bar v_0)\to(V,\bar v)$; applying it with $W=V$ supplies the required object of the affine full subcategory.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring): affine opens form a basis of the etale neighbourhoods

proof.text: Write $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ for the ambient pointed etale-neighbourhood category and $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}\subset\mathcal N$ for its full subcategory of affine objects. Initiality of the inclusion means that for every object $i$ of $\mathcal N$, the comma category $(\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}\downarrow i)$, whose objects are morphisms $a:j\to i$ with $j$ affine and whose morphisms $(j,a)\to(j',a')$ are morphisms $g:j\to j'$ with $a'\circ g=a$, is nonempty and connected. It is nonempty by step 1. For connectedness, given two objects $a_1:j_1\to i$ and $a_2:j_2\to i$ of this comma category, use the fibre-product clause of cofilteredness of $\mathcal N$ to obtain an object $k$ with morphisms $p_1:k\to j_1$, $p_2:k\to j_2$, and its equalizer clause applied to $a_1\circ p_1,a_2\circ p_2:k\to i$ to obtain $h:k'\to k$ with $a_1\circ p_1\circ h=a_2\circ p_2\circ h$. Step 1 supplies an affine object $j$ with a morphism $q:j\to k'$. Fullness of $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ makes $p_1\circ h\circ q:j\to j_1$ and $p_2\circ h\circ q:j\to j_2$ morphisms of the affine subcategory, and with $a=a_1\circ p_1\circ h\circ q=a_2\circ p_2\circ h\circ q$ they are morphisms $(j,a)\to(j_1,a_1)$ and $(j,a)\to(j_2,a_2)$ of the comma category; thus the two comma objects are joined by a zigzag through $(j,a)$, so the comma category is connected. Hence the affine inclusion is initial. The ambient category is cofiltered by the cited node, and the initial-full-subcategory criterion (1), whose hypothesis is step 1, then gives cofilteredness of the affine subcategory.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0BUC (lemma-cofinal-in-filtered, dual form) and Lemma Tag 04E7 (lemma-cofinal)

proof.text: Passing to opposite categories turns this initial inclusion into a final functor, so the canonical comparison identifies the colimit over the opposite-indexed affine neighbourhoods with the colimit over all pointed etale neighbourhoods. This is the stalk-colimit cofinality assertion.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04E7 (lemma-cofinal), applied to the opposite inclusion

blueprint_sketch.statement:
The full subcategory $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s}$ of affine pointed
etale neighbourhoods is initial in $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ and hence cofinal
for the opposite-indexed stalk colimit.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Given $(V,\bar v)$, choose an affine open $V_0\subseteq V$ containing the
image of $\bar v$; then $(V_0,\bar v)\to(V,\bar v)$ is a morphism. Given two
affine refinements, their fibre product over $V$ contains the lifted geometric
point; an affine open around that point refines both. These two facts give
nonemptiness and connectedness of every comma category required for
initiality.
